context:
Start with zero-effort wins (ruff rule, matrix entry) before building
new tooling. Each work unit is independently shippable - no need to
batch. Follow the existing CI structure in .github/workflows/test.yml.
description:
Codebase audit identified several categories of Windows issues that can
slip past the current CI matrix (Windows + Python 3.12 running fast tests
only). The codebase is reasonably Windows-aware (good pathlib usage, .exe
suffix handling, /proc/ fallbacks), but gaps remain in encoding, static
analysis, and integration test coverage on Windows.

Key findings from audit:
- ~6 open() calls in core/dryrun.py missing encoding="utf-8" (silent
  data corruption on Windows where default is cp1252)
- 3 os.access(path, os.X_OK) checks that are no-ops on Windows
- Integration tests (integration-smoke, test-package, pyspark) run
  Ubuntu-only - test-package uses bash-isms (source activate)
- Only Python 3.12 tested on Windows; 3.10 has different encoding defaults
- No static analysis catches Windows anti-patterns pre-merge

anti_patterns.dont: add Windows-only workarounds with sys.platform checks scattered through business logic
make integration tests conditional on platform
anti_patterns.why: fix the tests to be cross-platform instead

anti_patterns.dont: use continue-on-error: true for Windows jobs
anti_patterns.why: that hides failures instead of catching them

deferrals.reason:
The full integration suite (not just smoke) on Windows would add
significant CI time. Defer until Windows smoke tests are stable
and we have data on what additional issues the full suite catches.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] conditional-unmet: Gated on Windows smoke tests being stable with supporting data; no tracked item confirms that threshold was reached.
deferrals.summary: Run full integration suite on Windows

deferrals.reason:
A @pytest.mark.windows_sensitive marker for tests that exercise
platform-dependent code. Useful for targeted local testing but
requires ongoing discipline to apply. Revisit after w7 establishes
which tests are actually platform-sensitive.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] conditional-unmet: Revisit conditioned on w7 test-sensitivity findings from the same now-done item; no evidence of a concrete need or open tracking.

preserves.behavior: All existing tests continue to pass on Linux/macOS (no regressions)
CI time for the common case (Ubuntu PR) does not increase
Windows matrix entries use fail-fast: false to avoid masking issues

verifications.command: uv run ruff check benchbox/ --select PLW1514
verifications.description: Ruff catches open() calls without encoding

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests -m fast -q --tb=short

verifications.expected: Zero matches or all wrapped in platform check

Add Windows + Python 3.10 to CI test matrix
